dedupe_keys.name: space weather and critical infrastructures findings and outlook jrc eur 28237 2016

description: This JRC report records the findings of a November 2016 workshop in Ispra on how space weather threatens critical infrastructure in space and on the ground and how Europe and the United States are preparing. Elisabeth Krausmann of the Joint Research Centre, Emmelie Andersson of the Swedish Civil Contingencies Agency, Mark Gibbs of the UK Met Office and William Murtagh of the NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center wrote it as EUR 28237. It reviews the state of space weather science, known vulnerabilities and risk reduction by sector, national risk management and forecasting, response and recovery, and closes with recommendations. Its findings include that an extreme event could overwhelm one nation's response capacity, that operators should look for hidden dependencies such as GNSS timing, that gaps in physical and impact modelling limit early warning, and that 24/7 forecasting now exists in Europe and the USA. Coverage is Europe and North America. Format and access: a free 32-page PDF with participant list and agenda. Licence: European Union, reuse with acknowledgement. Caveats: it summarises expert discussion and is now dated. It frames hazard exposure, emergency response and resilience studies of space weather impacts. Related catalogue records are the UK space weather reasonable worst-case scenarios and the Lloyd's extreme space weather scenario.
